decision.chose: write directly to the main tree with a scoped hold + smoke test
decision.why: the change is small and purely additive (two edited files, one new page); the worktree pool doc itself says a small fix doesn't need its own worktree, and the three pool slots look stuck rather than about to free; minion rules forbid git add/commit in the main tree either way, so landing is the same file-write either path

log.msg: CAVEAT: edited Disclosure.js, content.css, Disclosure/page.js and Disclosure/readme.md, and added variants/page.js, directly in the main tree WITHOUT running Server/hold.mjs first — missed the reload-hold step while focused on the worktree-unavailable fallback. All edits are additive (new optional classes/keys; v1's own rendering path is untouched) and node --check passed on every .js file immediately after each edit, so the window of a broken intermediate state was small, but this should have been held. No sign the owner hit it (server logs not checked for a live request during that window).

Fixed two real bugs found only by measuring, not by eyeballing the screenshot: (1) marker-chevron/marker-twirl's open state fell back to the base rule's plain "−" glyph instead of rotating their own glyph, because I'd only set `transform` on the [open] rule, not `content`, at equal CSS specificity — fixed by repeating `content` in the [open] rule. (2) scheme-dark's title text rendered at rgb(63,63,63) on a rgb(35,38,45) background (1.44:1 contrast, far under the 4.5:1 floor) even though the container had `color:#fff`, because something more specific was setting the title's own color — fixed with an explicit summary/title/icon selector. Both confirmed via a small Playwright contrast/computed-style check in the scratchpad, not by re-eyeballing a screenshot.

gap-none (rounded per-item corners + zero gap) would have pinched at the touching corners per the layout skill's own rule — fixed the same way `flush` does: square the touching corners and add a divider when gap-none is used.
